name: Tweed Heads
timezone_note: Tweed Heads is NSW, so it observes daylight saving (AEDT, UTC+11); Coolangatta, a few hundred metres north in Queensland, stays on AEST (UTC+10). The Tweed Regional Gallery states it runs on DST, one hour ahead of Queensland during daylight saving.

facts: Tweed Heads is a coastal city at the mouth of the Tweed River in the Northern Rivers region of NSW; it is the northernmost town in NSW (Wikipedia, Tweed Heads).
Tweed Heads and Coolangatta (Queensland, part of Gold Coast City) are twin towns on the border; buildings and roads span it and it is often not obvious which state you are in (Wikivoyage).
Tweed Heads and neighbouring suburbs are part of the Gold Coast urban area but lie in Tweed Shire, headquartered in Murwillumbah (Wikivoyage).
Wikipedia gives distances from Tweed Heads: Gold Coast 34 km, Byron Bay 66 km, Brisbane 103 km, Lismore 99 km, Sydney 830 km.

Murwillumbah is a town on the Tweed River in the south-eastern foothills of the McPherson Range, in the Tweed Volcano valley and near Mount Warning (Wikipedia, Murwillumbah). Placement.json gives it 23 km from Tweed Heads.
Tweed Heads shares a tourism-heavy economy with Coolangatta given its proximity to the Gold Coast (Wikipedia).
Tweed Heads was the location of the fictional town Porpoise Spit in the 1994 film Muriel's Wedding (Wikipedia).

category_note: Tweed Heads is the border town and base, so city per proposal; the span is a town plus a valley, not a park.

description_facts.fact: Wollumbin (Mount Warning) rises to 1,157 m above sea level from World Heritage-listed Wollumbin National Park, a remnant central vent of an ancient volcano, viewable from the surrounding massive crater (caldera).
Wollumbin is highly significant to Aboriginal people, particularly the Bundjalung nation, as a place of sacred ceremonies.
Tweed River named by John Oxley, October 1823; first European settlers were cedar cutters in 1844; later dairy, sugar cane, bananas and fishing.

Point Danger Light, also the Captain Cook Memorial Light, is an active lighthouse on the headland between Coolangatta and Tweed Heads marking the NSW-Queensland border; built 1971; claims to be the first lighthouse to experiment with a laser light source.
The border runs parallel to the beach for some kilometres before ending at the headland north of the Tweed River mouth; it is the 19th-century survey line of the watershed.

Fingal Head has a round sandstone lighthouse inaugurated in 1878 (tower only 7 m high), part of a series of five built 1878-1880; the headland gives one of few spots near the Gold Coast protected from northerly winds.

whyVisit_candidates.subject: Wollumbin (Mount Warning) and the Tweed caldera, with the rainforest of Wollumbin National Park
whyVisit_candidates.photographable: Yes: the peak is a distinctive volcanic plug and is viewable from many points around the caldera (NPWS names Cudgen Nature Reserve, Border Ranges, Nightcap, Cape Byron). Placement photo exists: 'Mount Warning, NSW - panoramio.jpg' (2592x1936, accepted by Lens).
whyVisit_candidates.status_fact: NPWS: 'Wollumbin (Mount Warning) summit track and Aboriginal Place remains closed. Decisions about the future of the summit track will be made by NPWS in accordance with the wishes of Aboriginal custodians.' Do NOT write 'climb'. The park is open; the short Lyrebird track (rainforest walk) is a highlight, with Breakfast Creek camping and Korrumbyn Creek picnic area.

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Walk in the Margaret Olley Art Centre
whyVisit_candidates.subject: Tweed Regional Gallery and Margaret Olley Art Centre, Murwillumbah
whyVisit_candidates.photographable: Yes: Commons 'Tweed Regional Gallery 01.jpeg' is in skeptic.json. The Art Centre is a re-creation of Olley's Sydney workspace (Wikivoyage).
facts: Wikivoyage: 2 Mistral Road (corner Tweed Valley Way), contemporary international, national and regional exhibits, houses the Margaret Olley centre (re-creation of her Sydney workspace) and cafe; Free.

Official gallery page: open 10 am - 4 pm Wednesday to Sunday; entry free; daily guided tours start 11:30 am (about 45-55 min); the gallery runs on daylight saving time, an hour ahead of Queensland in summer. Cafe 10-4 Wed-Fri and 9-4 weekends (from search summary of the official page; verify the weekend hours).
The Rail Trail's Murwillumbah section connects to the gallery (rail trail site).

whyVisit_candidates.reason: Ride the Northern Rivers Rail Trail
whyVisit_candidates.subject: The Murwillumbah to Crabbes Creek section of the Northern Rivers Rail Trail
whyVisit_candidates.photographable: Yes, but no photo is named in the inputs; Lens must find one (trail, bridge or tunnel).
facts: 24 km section from the heritage-listed Murwillumbah Railway Station via the gallery, then Stokers Siding, Burringbar and Mooball to Crabbes Creek.
Surface is a blend of sealed sections and compacted gravel; the trail is described as accessible, with bridges and tunnels along it.

The whole trail will be 132 km when completed; Murwillumbah-Crabbes Creek (24 km) and Casino-Lismore (29.7 km) sections are open (as of the cached site page, which also mentions a 2023 event, so the page may be dated).
Walk, ride or run; the site lists bike hire and shuttle services.

whyVisit_alternates.subject: Point Danger Lighthouse and Fingal Head: the Captain Cook Memorial Light between Tweed Heads and Coolangatta, and the Fingal Head sandstone lighthouse and beach
whyVisit_alternates.photographable: Yes: Commons 'Point Danger and Tweed River mouth, Tweed Heads IMGP1702.jpg' is the Lens skyline/header pick; use a different file for the reason if the header uses it.

whyVisit_note: The three candidates are distinct (volcanic scenery, an art gallery, a cycling trail) and the headland/beach reason is the alternate; the three above are strongest by coverage in the inputs. Cabarita Beach and Kingscliff are surf and estuary beaches with no sourced detail beyond Wikipedia; I did not fetch them.

goodToKnow_candidates.tip: The Wollumbin summit track is closed. NPWS closed the summit track and Aboriginal Place and the future of the track will be decided with Aboriginal custodians; the park's rainforest Lyrebird track, picnic areas and Breakfast Creek camping remain. Check park alerts before driving out. The entrance gate may close from 5 PM in winter and 6 PM in summer (placement.json hours; not re-verified).

Gold Coast Airport (OOL, Coolangatta) is about 5 km from Tweed Heads and is a low-cost carrier hub (AirAsia X, Jetstar, others) but not a 24-hour airport; Brisbane is about 65 min by the Pacific Motorway. The border sits in the built-up area, and in summer Queensland does not observe daylight saving, so the clock changes an hour across the street; the gallery and other NSW operators run on NSW time.

Rail Trail logistics: the open Tweed section is 24 km one way from Murwillumbah Railway Station to Crabbes Creek, so plan a return shuttle or bike hire (the site lists bike hire and transport services). Murwillumbah is about 23 km inland by road from Tweed Heads (the Tweed Valley Way is the old Pacific Highway). Check the trail site's current alerts page before you go.

best_time.alt_whale_months_note: Whale watching (humpbacks) June to October/early November; southbound calves from Point Danger in October and November per a guide.
climate_facts: Wikipedia (BoM, Murwillumbah Bray Park): mean max 25.8 C, mean min 14.4 C, annual rainfall 1,581.5 mm for Tweed Heads.

Travel sources: shoulder seasons most comfortable, early April to mid-November suggested; December-February is hot with higher prices and bigger crowds; winter mild (one June guide gives 11-20 C, for the Gold Coast not Tweed specifically).
best_time.bestTimeBlurb_draft: Autumn and spring ({months}) are warm and drier, good for the rail trail and walks in the hills; humpback whales pass the headlands between June and November, and summer is hot and busy.
best_time.bestTimeBlurb_caveat: Southern-hemisphere months written. Draft blurb has no per-month rainfall figure; Tweed Heads is subtropical and the wet season is usually summer into early autumn (not sourced here: unverified). The blurb must carry exactly one {months} placeholder.

seasonalTags: whale migration Jun-Nov is a real recurring pattern; Tweed-specific peak not verified (blogs say Aug-Sep or Jul-Sep).
